# Mac
## Checking macOS version
::: {.screenshot-steps}

1. Click the Apple menu in the top-left corner of your screen.

    ![The Apple menu, expanded](/images/macos-version/01-apple-menu.png)

2. Choose **About This Mac**.

    ![The About This Mac option highlighted](/images/macos-version/02-about-this-mac.png)

3. Your version number appears under the macOS name.

    ![Version number shown as macOS Sequoia 15.7.7](/images/macos-version/03-version-number.png)

:::

## Download R based on your macOS version 
1. Go to [the R for macOS Installation site](https://cran.r-project.org)

![R for macOS site](/images/04-rmacos.png)


2. Determine the appropriate version of R 

| Chip | macOS | Download |
|---|---|---|
| M1, M2, M3, M4 | 14 or later | the `arm64` file |
| M1, M2, M3, M4 | 13 or earlier | update macOS first, then the `arm64` file |
| Intel | 11 or later | the `x86_64` file |

: Which installer to download {tbl-colwidths="[25,25,50]"}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Can't update macOS?
If you cannot update macOS, you can download the `x86_64` file instead. 
:::

3. Click on the appropriate version, and the download will start automatically

## Install R 

::: {.screenshot-steps}

1. Open Finder

    ![The Apple menu, expanded](/images/05-open-finder.png)

2. Open `Downloads` folder

    ![The About This Mac option highlighted](/images/06-downloads.png)

3. Click on the package, and follow the guide

    ![Version number shown as macOS Sequoia 15.7.7](/images/07-installer.png)

4. When it's complete, you'll get a popup asking if you want to move it to trash. You can safely do this, it does not affect anything.

    ![Version number shown as macOS Sequoia 15.7.7](/images/08-trash.png)

:::
